messages:
maya (product): Quick thread — need to prioritize a pricing/packaging plan for reserved capacity + new tiered rate limits. Two enterprise asks (Acme, BetaX). Can we do a short RICE + sequencing callout so PM/Eng/Finance agree on an MVP?
ankur (pm): +1. Options to compare: A) Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit + SLA) B) Soft-reserved + burst credits C) Tiered rate limits (PLG-focused). RICE sounds right.
tom (eng-lead): Engineering note: dedicated reserved demands billing changes, dedicated pool orchestration, quota enforcement at the edge, and changes to autoscaler. Ballpark: 8 dev-weeks + infra (parallel tasks) but expect cross-team dependencies.
sophia (sales): Field context: Acme will only sign with a dedicated pool + latency SLA. BetaX cares more about predictable unit costs and burst credits, not necessarily dedicated GPUs. Acme ARR ~ $450k/yr if we can meet SLA.
alexa (finance): Risk profile: reserved commits = upfront revenue but utilization risk. Need utilization scenarios (70/80/50%) to model net margin. Also revenue recognition and capacity procurement timing to consider.
ben (devx): Suggest a pragmatic rollout: ship tiered rate limits (low effort, big PLG upside) + a soft-reserved variant (virtual quota + priority routing + burst credits). That avoids big infra changes initially.
maya (product): I'll sketch a quick RICE for comparison — throwing numbers out to provoke discussion.
```
Option                    Reach   Impact  Confidence  Effort(weeks)   RICE_score
Reserved (dedicated)      2/mo    8       0.6           40           (2*8*0.6)/40 = 0.24
Soft-reserved + burst     50/mo   6       0.7            8           (50*6*0.7)/8 = 26.25
Tiered rate limits (PLG) 200/mo   4       0.9            3           (200*4*0.9)/3 = 240
```
ankur (pm): The math shows tiered rate limits and soft-reserved >> dedicated for RICE, but double-check Reach for reserved (likely lower). Also consider strategic value (enterprise logos).
tom (eng-lead): Agree on math direction. But reserved effort is probably higher once you add legal/ops/console/monitoring — say 60 effort-weeks across teams -> RICE drops further.
sophia (sales): Even if RICE low, dedicated reserved has outsized sales enablement value for enterprise GTM. We should treat it as a strategic bet but only fund after validating demand through soft-reserved pilots.
lina (legal): Dedicated reserved requires contract templates + SLA clauses + breach remedies. Estimate 4–6 weeks review and negotiation for the first template.
alexa (finance): Proposed staged approach: Phase 1 = Tiered rate limits + Soft-reserved/burst credits (fast, revenue capture, low capital). Phase 2 = Dedicated reserved (only if committed ARR >= threshold and utilization scenarios vetted).
ben (devx): Implementation notes: For Phase 1 we need: (1) per-tenant rate limiter config in edge (2) Console UI for tiers + credit balances (3) billing metric for burst consumption. I estimate ~3 sprints cross-functional for MVP.
maya (product): Launch criteria for Phase 1 (tiered + soft-reserved): 1) Edge enforcement + quota API GA, 2) Console tier screen + billing hook, 3) Docs + pricing page, 4) Pilot with BetaX or similar, 5) Observability: token-level cost + priority latency dashboard.
ops-bot: Reminder: Planning meeting scheduled Thu 10:30am — calendar invite sent.
maya (product): Decision suggestion: prioritize Tiered rate limits + Soft-reserved/burst (Phase 1). Defer Dedicated reserved as Phase 2 gated by validated demand and legal/finance signoff.
ankur (pm): +1. I'll own the RICE + stakeholder memo and add the gating metrics for promoting Phase 2.
tom (eng-lead): I'll scope engineering epics for Phase 1 and return with a sprint-by-sprint plan by EOD Friday.
sophia (sales): I'll line up BetaX pilot and surface 2 other potential pilots.
alexa (finance): I'll run utilization scenarios and define the ARR threshold and pricing floor for Phase 2.
lina (legal): I'll draft the first contract template and SLA checklist for review.
maya (product): Great — action items captured. We'll reconvene after the scoping doc. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
